entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Luigi Maria D'Albertis was an Italian naturalist and explorer who, in 1875, became the first Italian to chart the Fly River in what is now called Papua New Guinea. He undertook three voyages up this river from 1875 to 1877, where the first was conducted in the steamer SS Ellengowan and the other two in a smaller ship named the "Neva" which was chartered from the Government of New South Wales. Throughout the three voyages, D'Albertis was consistently involved in skirmishes with the various indigenous people living along the river, using rifle-fire, rockets and dynamite to intimidate and, on occasions, kill these local people.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: D'Albertis's expeditions to the Fly River had significant regional impact in Papua New Guinea, contributing to European exploration and colonization of the region. His actions also led to conflicts with indigenous populations, resulting in loss of life and displacement.
